text: Beginning three-host audit; compare restored historical logs with current activity and preserve service continuity.
Starting database host audit, including restored logs and backup dependencies.
Starting CI host audit, including release and archive paths.
Removed unrestricted deploy sudo rsync (CI uses tar); gated agency support environment and destructive purge behind WordPress admin authentication and nonce to prevent unauthenticated access/CSRF.
Hardened customer export: root uses private temporary data and creates final output without clobber as the requesting user, closing a predictable-filename symlink overwrite.

jpark contractor is not in staff directory, has no successful login in retained logs but retains password and passwordless sudo; locked password, removed sudo and denied SSH including keys, without deleting evidence or other users.
Disabled retired or unlisted contractor jpark on CI, preserving files; no retained successful sessions found.
Denied server-side execution in user uploads while retaining image and form uploads; tested nginx configuration.
Mid-shift CI monitoring: inspect new sessions, maintenance and release state.
Mid-shift db audit includes dump, settlement, SSH, invoice changes.
Mid-shift web status: monitor authentication, payout and release related writable locations.
Unlisted former contractor also had a WordPress administrator account; revoked role, reset its credential and destroyed sessions, retaining account/content.
Continuing live monitoring of web-01.
Blocked serving backup/source dump/environment filename extensions; found nonsecret historical source .bak, no observed requests for it.

Plaintext SQL billing and shop dumps were world-readable to local users. Restricted archive directory and existing dumps; job now uses umask 077. No evidence yet that unauthorized staff read secrets; do not conflate exposure with proven read.

Correction: plaintext dump files had mode 644 but parent directory was root:root 750, so unprivileged users could not traverse it. Tightened defense-in-depth to 700/600; no evidence of plaintext access inferred.
Routine database recheck: jobs and account activity reviewed.

GitHub token was embedded in group/world-readable shared Git config; moved current URL credential to deploy-only store and kept shared remote URL clean. rotate-secret deploy-token later writes config and must be re-sanitized into credential store; investigate actual access rather than assume disclosure.
Continued CI monitoring after credential isolation.
Routine web recheck; no confirmed compromise; user-facing and jobs continue.
Observed scheduled payout batch and next dump; continue monitoring.
Verified new private dump reaches CI and releases persist.
Authenticated support environment now provides the nonce for authorized POST purge so the support function remains usable.
Late-shift web monitoring: inspect new sessions, attacks, and scheduled jobs.
